verdict.rationale: Supermemory documents container-tag isolation as a hard boundary between tenants and mentions SOC 2/HIPAA BAA compliance and an 'independent audit of security controls,' which gives some coarse-grained tenant separation and compliance-level audit assurance, but there is no evidence of role-based access control, fine-grained read/write policies, or per-user access-control lists, and no audit-log/trail feature for tracking who accessed which memories. Community evidence even notes the MCP endpoint uses a URL-as-key with no signin, undercutting confidence in fine-grained access governance for that surface. Missing for 10: RBAC/roles, explicit read/write policy enforcement, ACLs beyond container tags, and access audit logs/trails.
